cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to believers living as exiles, scattered across a bunch of regions (1 Pet 1:1). He just told them to repay insults with blessing, not with more insults (1 Pet 3:9). Now he asks them a question: "Who can harm you if you are zealous for what is good?"
Zealous means FIRED UP, like me when the oven timer dings. But Peter's honest here: even if you're fired up for good, you could still suffer for doing what's right.

cards.question: When someone suffers for doing what's right, what does Peter call them?

cards.text: Then Peter says, "Do not fear what they fear; do not be shaken." Friend, I lived in a junk drawer for YEARS, and every time somebody yanked it open looking for tape, I got SHAKEN.

cards.question: Instead of fearing, Peter tells the believers to sanctify Christ as Lord. Where?

cards.text: Next, Peter says to always be prepared to give a defense to everyone who asks. Always prepared? Baker, I once showed up to my own bakery without my APRON.

cards.question: When someone asks, what does Peter say the believers should be ready to explain?

answers.text: The reason for the hope in them

cards.question: Peter says to answer anyone who asks with gentleness and respect.

cards.text: Gentle. Respectful. Not like the group chat where somebody answers everything in ALL CAPS. And Peter says to keep a clear conscience while they do it.

cards.question: Some people will still slander the believers. What does Peter say their good behavior in Christ will do to those people?

answers.text: Turn the whole town against them

cards.text: Then Peter says suffering may come, if it's God's will. But not all suffering is the same.

cards.question: If suffering comes and it's God's will, which does Peter say is better?

cards.text: Then Peter points the believers to Christ. Because Christ also suffered for sins.

cards.question: Peter says Christ suffered for sins. How many times?
Christ suffered as the righteous for the unrighteous. What does Peter say it was for?

cards.text: Then Peter says it plainly: He was put to death in the body. But Peter's not done with that sentence.

cards.question: After Christ was put to death in the body, Peter says He stayed dead.

cards.text: Then Peter says Christ also went and preached to the spirits in prison. Spirits who disobeyed long ago.

cards.question: Those spirits disobeyed long ago, while God waited patiently. In whose days?

cards.text: God waited patiently while the ark was being built. Me? I can't wait patiently for ONE batch to cool.

cards.question: In the ark, only ___ souls were saved through water.

cards.text: Then Peter says the water of Noah's day symbolizes something for his readers too.

cards.question: What does Peter say the water of Noah's day symbolizes?
Peter says baptism is about washing dirt off the body.
If baptism isn't about dirt, what does Peter call it?

answers.text: The pledge of a clear conscience toward God
A way to earn a place in heaven
A promise to keep every single law

cards.text: And it saves through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God. Put to death, made alive, and now at God's right hand.

cards.question: Peter says angels, authorities and powers are what to Jesus now?

findings.problem: The card spends words defining 'zealous' ('Zealous means FIRED UP'). That word should get a dictionary pop-up instead of card space.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The card retells 'Gentle. Respectful.' from 1 Peter 3:15 as well as the clear conscience from 3:16, but it cites only 1 Peter 3:16. It should cite 1 Peter 3:15-16.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The second sentence ('Put to death, made alive, and now at God's right hand') retells 1 Peter 3:18, but the card cites only 1 Peter 3:21-22. Either the citation should run 1 Peter 3:18-22, or the sentence should go, since it also works as a recap.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup says the water 'symbolizes something for his readers too.' That points to something present in the readers' lives and rules out the wrong answers on card 11 ('The Red Sea crossing', 'The Jordan crossing'), which are past events. Those wrong answers are also not the same kind of thing as baptism.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answers are one-time historical events, while the right answer (Baptism) is an ongoing practice. They are not the same kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The right answer ('The pledge of a clear conscience toward God') uses near-verbatim Bible wording. The wrong answers are plain modern paraphrase, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 5 of the 6 choice cards in this stop, with only 1 true or false and no fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 6 of the 9 choice cards in this stop, against 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The story cards in this stop are almost all flat narration with no Papa Dorin voice (cards 1, 4, 6, 10 and 14). Card 8 is the only joke. Card 1 ('Then Peter points the believers to Christ. Because Christ also suffered for sins.') reads stripped down. Reverence limits what he can joke about here, but his storyteller voice, wonder and reactions should still come through.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
